meta.summary: Actors (agents + systems) are nodes. Click a flow to trace the handoffs — edge labels are the real mechanism (CLI command / endpoint / marker), cited to file:line.

nodes.label: ACT Server
nodes.detail: Coordination server: tasks, projects, validation, PVM, REST + Socket.io.

nodes.label: Runner (spawner)
nodes.detail: Spawns one Node process per swarm role; polls for tasks, reports completion.

nodes.label: TUI · Orchestrator
nodes.detail: The NesTTY window process; parses Planner markers, runs the coordination loops.

flows.label: Greenfield INTAKE → project creation → BUILD
flows.summary: Human types into the TUI; the Planner is the only agent that responds and runs a conversational 5-question intake (prompt-only). On explicit confirmation it emits a PROJECT_BRIEF: text marker in its own turn; the orchestrator's messageOwnershipLoop scans the finished Planner message, parses the JSON, and POSTs it to the ACT server which stores the project record. The orchestrator then clears intakeMode and fires a BUILD-mode trigger turn back at the Planner. Edges are code-enforced except the 5Q conversation and the 'Ready to start?' hard-stop, which live only in planner.go prompt text.

steps.label: human text → runAgentTurn(planner)
steps.detail: HandleHumanInput routes every human message to a Planner turn via runAgentTurn(ctx, sessionID, "planner", text, true) at orchestrator.go:242.

steps.label: 5-question INTAKE, one topic per turn
steps.detail: The 5-thing conversational intake (description/techStack/constraints/successCriteria/agentsInvolved, one topic per turn, no form-dump) exists only as instruction text in basePlannerPrompt at planner.go:37-41.

steps.label: summarize → 'Ready to start?' → STOP
steps.detail: The hard-stop rule — summarize, ask 'Ready to start?', end the turn, and emit PROJECT_BRIEF only in the NEXT turn after explicit confirmation — is prompt text at planner.go:45; nothing in code enforces the turn separation.

steps.label: emit 'PROJECT_BRIEF: {json}' marker in reply text
steps.detail: On confirmation the Planner writes the literal PROJECT_BRIEF: line (planner.go:47-48); the orchestrator's messageOwnershipLoop detects the finished Planner message and, while intakeMode is true, dispatches handleProjectBrief at orchestrator.go:1210-1212.

steps.label: parseProjectBrief() extracts + parses JSON
steps.detail: handleProjectBrief calls parseProjectBrief(content) (orchestrator.go:1544); parseProjectBrief keys on the PROJECT_BRIEF: marker, falling back to any JSON containing successCriteria, at orchestrator.go:3050-3056.

steps.label: POST /api/projects (CreateProject)
steps.detail: handleProjectBrief calls client.CreateProject(...) at orchestrator.go:1578, which POSTs to /api/projects (client.go:552-562); the server builds a ProjectRecord and stores it in the projects map at index.ts:383-407.

steps.label: projects.set(name, project) + chronlog project_created
steps.detail: POST /api/projects writes projects.set(name, project) (index.ts:399) and appends a project_created event to the ChronologicalLog (index.ts:400-406).

steps.label: clear intakeMode → BUILD-mode trigger turn
steps.detail: After a successful POST the orchestrator sets intakeMode=false (orchestrator.go:1610) and fires fireWhenPlannerIdle with a renderBriefContext("build", ...) prompt that switches the Planner to BUILD mode (orchestrator.go:1628-1636).

flows.label: Brownfield INTAKE → 2-question variant → project creation
flows.summary: When detectProjectState finds no server project record but the directory has existing code, the orchestrator flips a brownfield flag, runs a deterministic scaffold + researcher enrichment to produce a codebase analysis, stashes it, and seeds the Planner with a 'CODEBASE ANALYSIS' intake turn. The Planner runs a 2-question variant (prompt-only) instead of the 5Q form, then follows the same PROJECT_BRIEF → POST /api/projects path; the stashed analysis is folded into AGENTS.md as a '## Codebase analysis' section. Detection, analysis pipeline, the CODEBASE ANALYSIS label, the POST, and the AGENTS.md fold are code-enforced; the 2-question conversation is prompt-only.

steps.label: detectProjectState → GET /api/projects/:name = 404 + existing code
steps.detail: detectProjectState calls client.GetProject(name) (orchestrator.go:260); on not-found it checks hasExistingCode(projectDir) and sets o.brownfield=true at orchestrator.go:317-320. GET /api/projects/:name returns 404 for an unknown project at index.ts:414-416.

steps.label: deterministicScaffold + researcher enrichment → analysis
steps.detail: runBrownfieldOnboard builds the analysis via deterministicScaffold (orchestrator.go:355, runs `act codebase onboard` at :401) then runResearcherEnrichment (orchestrator.go:363), stashing the result in o.codebaseAnalysis at orchestrator.go:379-381.

steps.label: seed 'CODEBASE ANALYSIS' intake turn (fireWhenPlannerIdle)
steps.detail: renderBrownfieldIntake emits a turn carrying the literal CODEBASE ANALYSIS block (orchestrator.go:530-539) and fireWhenPlannerIdle delivers it to the Planner at orchestrator.go:387.

steps.label: 2-question variant (build-next? + don't-touch?)
steps.detail: The brownfield branch — skip the 5Q form, present analysis, ask only (1) what to build/change next and (2) what agents must NOT touch — is prompt text keyed on the 'CODEBASE ANALYSIS' block at planner.go:43; same 'Ready to start?' hard stop applies.

steps.label: emit 'PROJECT_BRIEF: {json}' (techStack from analysis)
steps.detail: Confirmation routes through the same intakeMode path: messageOwnershipLoop → handleProjectBrief at orchestrator.go:1210-1212; the brownfield branch keeps intakeMode true so the brief uses the shared handler (orchestrator.go:383-384).

steps.label: POST /api/projects (CreateProject)
steps.detail: handleProjectBrief calls client.CreateProject (orchestrator.go:1578 → client.go:552) hitting POST /api/projects which stores the ProjectRecord (index.ts:383-407) — identical to greenfield.

steps.label: fold analysis into AGENTS.md '## Codebase analysis'
steps.detail: Before POSTing, handleProjectBrief sets brief.CodebaseNotes = o.codebaseAnalysis (orchestrator.go:1569); writeAgentsMd renders it as a '## Codebase analysis' section when non-empty at agents_md.go:31-32.

flows.label: Decompose → CREATE_TASK dispatch → lazy swarm spawn
flows.summary: In BUILD mode the Planner decomposes the brief into 3-8 tasks and emits CREATE_TASK: text markers. The orchestrator's messageOwnershipLoop parses + content-hash-dedups them, lazily spawns the Tier-2 swarm (one Node act-runner.mjs per requested role) on the first batch, then POSTs each task to /api/tasks where the server creates it and runs assignOptimalAgent for capability-based routing. Two-pass dependency resolution PATCHes title-string deps to server IDs. Decomposition rules are prompt-only; parsing, dedup, spawn, POST, assignment, and dep-resolution are code-enforced.

steps.label: decompose brief into 3-8 tasks (@task/@success_criteria)
steps.detail: Step 2 of basePlannerPrompt instructs decomposition into 3-8 tasks each using only @task and @success_criteria SPIL sections, with role/capability matching rules, at planner.go:85-96.

steps.label: emit 'CREATE_TASK: {json}' markers in reply text
steps.detail: The Planner writes CREATE_TASK: lines as plain reply text (planner.go:95-96); when not in intake mode messageOwnershipLoop dispatches handlePlannerTaskDirectives at orchestrator.go:1214.

steps.label: parseCreateTaskDirectives + content-hash dedup
steps.detail: handlePlannerTaskDirectives calls parseCreateTaskDirectives (orchestrator.go:1672; brace-counting parser at :2988) then taskBatchHash + checkAndRecordDispatchHash to drop duplicate re-emitted batches at orchestrator.go:1696-1713.

steps.label: lazy StartSwarm on first batch (spawn node act-runner.mjs/role)
steps.detail: On the first batch, if the runner isn't already running, the orchestrator filters specs by the project's agentsInvolved and calls runnerSpawner.StartSwarm (orchestrator.go:1730-1739); StartSwarm spawns one `node act-runner.mjs --agent-id … --role …` subprocess per spec (spawner.go:58-92, exec.Command at :123).

steps.label: POST /api/tasks per task (CreateTask)
steps.detail: For each parsed task the orchestrator calls client.CreateTask (orchestrator.go:1783) → POST /api/tasks (client.go:341-350); the server fail-closes on empty title/description then taskCoordinator.createTask(req.body) at index.ts:516-532.

steps.label: createTask + assignOptimalAgent (capability routing)
steps.detail: POST /api/tasks stores the task and, when no agent is pre-assigned, calls taskCoordinator.assignOptimalAgent(task.id) to capability-match it to a registered runner, emitting task_assigned, at index.ts:532-560.

steps.label: Pass 2: PATCH /api/tasks/:id/dependencies (title→ID)
steps.detail: Because the Planner can only name deps by title, a second pass resolves sibling titles to server-assigned IDs and calls client.SetTaskDependencies (orchestrator.go:1799-1813) → PATCH /api/tasks/:id/dependencies (client.go:375-383).

flows.label: Swarm task execution (spawn → bootstrap → complete → submit-for-validation)
flows.summary: Runner is spawned by the orchestrator on the first CREATE_TASK batch (one Node process per swarm role). Each runner self-registers, polls /api/tasks/assigned, and on a hit spawns the swarm agent (act-agent headless or claude-code). Self-bootstrap is NOT via `act context`: the runner fetches the brief over HTTP and injects it into the prompt directly. The swarm agent does the work, then the RUNNER (not the agent) calls /complete and /submit-for-validation over HTTP — the in-prompt `act task complete` text is prompt-only redundancy.

steps.label: spawn one Node process per swarm role (StartSwarm)
steps.detail: Orchestrator.handlePlannerTaskDirectives calls o.runnerSpawner.StartSwarm(specs) on the CREATE_TASK batch (internal/app/orchestrator.go:1737); Spawner.startOneLocked runs exec.Command(nodeBin, scriptPath, --agent-id, --name, --role, --backend) (internal/runner/spawner.go:113-122).

steps.label: POST /api/agents/register (self-register, 409 self-heal)
steps.detail: runner register() posts /api/agents/register, deregisters+retries on HTTP 409 stale registration (act-agent/runner/act-runner.mjs:129-154); server handler at server/src/index.ts:265.

steps.label: poll GET /api/tasks/assigned?agent_id&project (5s loop)
steps.detail: runner getTask() GETs /api/tasks/assigned scoped to agent_id+project in the coordination loop (act-agent/runner/act-runner.mjs:162-169, loop at 808-810); server route server/src/index.ts:590.

steps.label: spawn act-agent --agent --role --prompt (or claude-code)
steps.detail: runAgentActAgent execFile(AGENT_CLI, [--agent, AGENT_ID, --role, AGENT_ROLE, --prompt, prompt]) (act-agent/runner/act-runner.mjs:235-240); runAgent picks claude-code vs act-agent by BACKEND (227-232). Recipient role is whichever of developer/frontend/backend/qa/researcher this runner was spawned as.

steps.label: inject AGENTS.md brief into prompt (NOT `act context`)
steps.detail: CLAUDE.md claims swarm self-bootstrap via `act-agent context <id>`, but the runner never calls `act context` (no such call in act-runner.mjs). Instead fetchAgentBrief() GETs /api/projects/:name/briefs/:agentId and buildTaskPrompt prepends it as `## Project Brief` (act-agent/runner/act-runner.mjs:543-545, 557, 614). Equivalent outcome, different mechanism than documented.

steps.label: prompt-instructed `act files claim` / `act task complete`
steps.detail: buildTaskPrompt's Workflow text tells the LLM to run `act files claim`, `act task complete`, `act files release` (act-agent/runner/act-runner.mjs:699-706). These are instructions in prompt text — the swarm agent may or may not execute them; the authoritative completion is the runner's own HTTP call below.

steps.label: POST /api/tasks/:id/complete (code-enforced, on process exit)
steps.detail: reportComplete() posts /api/tasks/${taskId}/complete with agentId/success/result regardless of whether the agent self-reported (act-agent/runner/act-runner.mjs:181-186); server route server/src/index.ts:708.

steps.label: POST /api/tasks/:id/submit-for-validation (on success)
steps.detail: reportComplete() then posts /api/tasks/${taskId}/submit-for-validation when success is true, feeding the Assurance/QA pipeline (act-agent/runner/act-runner.mjs:191-200); server route server/src/index.ts:838.

flows.label: File locking (claim / release)
flows.summary: File locking is prompt-only on the swarm side: the runner tells the swarm agent to run `act files claim`/`release`, and the act-agent CLI implements those as POST /api/files/claim and /release. There is no runner-side enforcement that the agent actually claims before editing — claiming depends on the LLM following the workflow text.

steps.label: prompt-instructed `act files claim <paths>` → POST /api/files/claim
steps.detail: The claim step exists only as Workflow prompt text the LLM is asked to run (act-agent/runner/act-runner.mjs:699). If the agent runs it, cli/act-cli.ts dispatches `files claim` → cmdFilesClaim → client POST /api/files/claim (cli/act-cli.ts:1191; client internal/act/client.go:166-173; server route server/src/index.ts:1072).

steps.label: prompt-instructed `act files release <paths>` → POST /api/files/release
steps.detail: Release is likewise prompt text, with an auto-release-on-complete fallback noted in the prompt (act-agent/runner/act-runner.mjs:706). CLI branch `files release` → client POST /api/files/release (cli/act-cli.ts:1205; internal/act/client.go:182-188; server route server/src/index.ts:1115).

flows.label: Tier 1 backend dispatch (in-process goroutine vs ACP host)
flows.summary: Each Tier-1 role (planner/observer/assurance/qa) is wired once at app.New() by a single switch on agents.<role>.backend in ~/.act.json. Empty/act-agent → in-process agent.NewAgent goroutine sharing the TUI session. External hosts (claude-code, antigravity/agy; codex/opencode stubbed) → acp.NewACPAgent, which spawns the external CLI over ACP via exec.Command. The /backend slash command flips the config.

steps.label: default branch → agent.NewAgent (in-process goroutine)
steps.detail: app.New() switch default case builds Tier1ToolsForRole + agent.NewAgent with HistoryThread for planner, HistoryNone for observer/assurance/qa (internal/app/app.go:104,110-137). These run in-process; HandleHumanInput → runAgentTurn → agentSvc.Run (orchestrator.go:242, 601).

steps.label: case claude-code/antigravity/agy/codex/opencode → acp.NewACPAgent
steps.detail: Same app.New() switch: backendChoice from cfg.Agents[agentName].Backend; case for external hosts calls acp.NewACPAgent(role, backendChoice, withShim, ...) (internal/app/app.go:90-110). ACP layer spawns the host via exec.Command — claudeCodeDefaults() or antigravityCLIDefaults(); codex/opencode return unimplemented (internal/acp/agent.go:547-557,561).

steps.label: external CLI drives the role's turns over ACP (Run)
steps.detail: ACPAgent.Run satisfies the same agent.Service contract as the in-process path, so orchestrator routing is backend-agnostic; per-role CLI allowlist enforced via the tier1 shim path (internal/acp/agent.go:182-186; withTier1ShimPath in app.go:108). Any Tier-1 role (planner/observer/assurance/qa) can be the dispatched role.

flows.label: Human → Planner → Server → Runner (intake + task dispatch framing)
flows.summary: Frames the swarm flow: human input goes ONLY to the Planner; the Planner emits PROJECT_BRIEF (intake) and CREATE_TASK (build) markers that the orchestrator parses and turns into REST calls (CreateProject, CreateTask). Other Tier-1 agents reach the Planner via InternalPromptMarker autoroute, never the human directly.

steps.label: HandleHumanInput → runAgentTurn(planner, fromHuman=true)
steps.detail: TUI's only human entry point routes to the Planner and clears the autoroute sliding window (internal/app/orchestrator.go:224-242). Planner is the sole role that sees human turns.

steps.label: PROJECT_BRIEF: marker → client.CreateProject → POST /api/projects
steps.detail: handleProjectBrief parses the PROJECT_BRIEF: JSON and calls client.CreateProject(...) (orchestrator.go:1542-1578); client POSTs /api/projects; server route server/src/index.ts:383. Marker is emitted only in a separate turn after human confirmation (prompt rule at orchestrator.go:537).

steps.label: CREATE_TASK: marker → client.CreateTask → POST /api/tasks
steps.detail: parseCreateTaskDirectives extracts balanced-brace CREATE_TASK JSON (orchestrator.go:2988-3052), handlePlannerTaskDirectives calls client.CreateTask per task (orchestrator.go:1783; client internal/act/client.go:341-350; server route server/src/index.ts:502).

steps.label: Tier-1 → Planner via InternalPromptMarker autoroute (≤5/10min)
steps.detail: Observer/Assurance/QA outputs trigger autoRoutePlannerV; non-human prompts get InternalPromptMarker prepended so the TUI hides them (orchestrator.go:580-585,682). Observer itself runs a 120s anomaly loop (observerLoop, orchestrator.go:171,185); Assurance verdict via SubmitVerdict and QA via SubmitSynthesis after their own turns (routeToAssurance orchestrator.go:2660; routeToQA orchestrator.go:2806).

flows.label: Validation (Assurance scoring)
flows.summary: Orchestrator polls the server for tasks awaiting validation every 10s, runs an Assurance turn that scores each @success_criteria with view/grep evidence, parses the JSON verdict (95% gate, fail-closed on empty criteria), and POSTs the verdict back to the server which moves the task to 'validated' (pass) or 'assigned' (fail).

steps.label: GET /api/tasks/pending-validation (10s poll)
steps.detail: validationPollLoop ticks every validationPollPeriod=10s (orchestrator.go:1991,2560) and checkPendingValidation calls client.GetPendingValidation -> GET /api/tasks/pending-validation?project= (client.go:466-471; server index.ts:632), then routeToAssurance runs the Assurance turn (orchestrator.go:2608,2613).

steps.label: score @success_criteria via view/grep (95% gate, fail-closed)
steps.detail: buildValidationPrompt instructs per-criterion view/grep verification and 'Pass = score >= 95' (orchestrator.go:3147-3169); parseValidationVerdict enforces passThreshold=95 AND fails closed when criteriaResults is empty (orchestrator.go:3094-3110).

steps.label: POST /api/tasks/:id/validation-verdict
steps.detail: routeToAssurance parses the Assurance reply and calls client.SubmitVerdict (orchestrator.go:2643,2662), which POSTs /api/tasks/:taskId/validation-verdict (client.go:572-581); the handler sets status 'validated' on pass or back to 'assigned' on fail and appends task_validated/task_validation_failed to ChronLog (index.ts:875-927).

steps.label: validation event surfaced in chat (coord poll 3s)
steps.detail: coordinationEventLoop polls /api/log every coordinationEventInterval=3s (orchestrator.go:686) and renders task_validated/task_validation_failed as system chat lines '✅ validation passed' / '❌ validation failed' (orchestrator.go:865-868).

flows.label: Synthesis & delivery (QA -> Planner -> human)
flows.summary: Orchestrator polls the server for validated tasks, runs a QA/Synthesizer turn that assembles the deliverable and emits SYNTHESIS_COMPLETE or NEED_CLARIFICATION, POSTs the outcome to the server (stamping metadata.synthesizedAt on complete), and the QA report auto-routes into a Planner turn whose output reaches the human via the chat.

steps.label: GET /api/tasks/validated (10s poll)
steps.detail: qaPollLoop ticks every 10s (orchestrator.go:2682); checkValidatedTasks calls client.GetValidatedTasks -> GET /api/tasks/validated?project= (client.go:477-482; server filters out tasks with metadata.synthesizedAt, index.ts:652-658), then routeToQA runs the QA turn (orchestrator.go:2733,2738).

steps.label: assemble deliverable -> SYNTHESIS_COMPLETE / NEED_CLARIFICATION
steps.detail: buildSynthesisPrompt asks QA to integrate the validated output (orchestrator.go:3173-3177); parseSynthesisResponse extracts kind from the SYNTHESIS_COMPLETE: marker or the NEED_CLARIFICATION: @agent regex, else 'in_progress' (orchestrator.go:3128-3137); markers are the prompt contract in qa_synthesizer.go:46-51.

steps.label: POST /api/tasks/:id/synthesis (kind=complete|need_clarification)
steps.detail: routeToQA calls client.SubmitSynthesis (orchestrator.go:2805) -> POST /api/tasks/:taskId/synthesis (client.go:593); on kind='complete' the server stamps task.metadata.synthesizedAt and appends synthesis_complete to ChronLog, on need_clarification appends synthesis_needs_clarification (index.ts:934-975).

steps.label: QA output autoroute -> Planner turn (InternalPromptMarker, !fromHuman)
steps.detail: messageOwnershipLoop routes a qa_synthesizer message via autoRoutePlannerV unless it is a NEED_CLARIFICATION addressed to a non-Planner (then maybeRouteQAClarification forwards to that agent's inbox and skips Planner) (orchestrator.go:1216-1251,2840+); the Planner turn is fired with fromHuman=false so the prompt is prefixed with InternalPromptMarker (orchestrator.go:584-585).

steps.label: Planner reply rendered in chat
steps.detail: The autorouted Planner turn runs via fireWhenPlannerIdle -> runAgentTurn (orchestrator.go:1350); the Planner is the only role that addresses the human and its reply renders without the InternalPromptMarker (orchestrator.go:577-585). Note: synthesis_complete also surfaces directly as a '🎁 synthesized' system line via the coord poll (orchestrator.go:869-872), so the human sees the delivery on two surfaces.

flows.label: Autoroute (Tier-1 output -> Planner)
flows.summary: Any non-Planner Tier-1 message (Observer/Assurance/QA) is wrapped with the InternalPromptMarker and fired as a Planner turn (fromHuman=false), variant-selected by trigger, and rate-limited by a sliding window of at most 5 fires per 10 minutes that is cleared on every human input.

steps.label: Observer/Assurance/QA message -> autoRoutePlannerV (variant-selected)
steps.detail: messageOwnershipLoop's role switch handles observer/assurance/qa/qa_synthesizer and calls autoRoutePlannerV; for assurance it picks variantPassVerdict/variantFailVerdict via parseValidationVerdict, else variantAnomaly (orchestrator.go:1216-1251). Planner replies are NOT auto-routed, breaking the loop (comment orchestrator.go:1234-1235).

steps.label: wrap prompt: InternalPromptMarker + fromHuman=false
steps.detail: autoRoutePlannerV builds the per-variant prompt (renderAutoRoutePrompt, orchestrator.go:1345,1356) and fires runAgentTurn with fromHuman=false, which prepends InternalPromptMarker so the injected prompt is hidden but the Planner's reply shows (orchestrator.go:565,584-585,682).

steps.label: sliding-window cap: <=5 fires / 10min, cleared on human input
steps.detail: autoRoutePlannerV prunes recentAutoRoutes to autoRouteWindow=10min and drops the fire when len >= autoTurnCap=5, logging autoroute_planner_dropped (orchestrator.go:1316-1331,1421,1427); HandleHumanInput resets o.recentAutoRoutes=nil (orchestrator.go:228).

flows.label: Observer watchdog → anomaly → autoroute → Planner
flows.summary: Observer polls the ACT server every 120s via its own act.Client, builds a status snapshot from four REST list endpoints, runs detectAnomalies, gates on a stable anomaly-set signature, runs an Observer LLM turn, and that turn's output is auto-routed into a Planner turn through the agent-message handler. The poll/gate/autoroute plumbing is all code-enforced; the actual anomaly detection rules are a Go port of observer.go's prompt rules (real code), and whether the Observer's narrative classifies an anomaly correctly is LLM-driven.

steps.label: 120s ticker → buildStatusSnapshot (GET /api/tasks,/api/agents,file-locks,/api/log)
steps.detail: observerLoop's time.NewTicker(observerInterval=120s) calls runObserverCheck, which constructs act.NewClient("observer",...) and calls buildStatusSnapshot — four parallel client calls ListTasks/ListAgents/GetFileLocks/GetLog(20) — at act-agent/internal/app/orchestrator.go:2013, :2049-2054, :2217-2220 (observerInterval at :1977).

steps.label: detectAnomalies(snapshot) + signature no-op gate (sha256 of category+task+agent)
steps.detail: detectAnomalies(snapshot) runs the 6 detection rules and the result set is hashed via anomalySignature; if the hash equals o.lastObserverPromptHash the cycle returns silently (skip), preventing repeat escalation, at act-agent/internal/app/orchestrator.go:2074, :2112-2128, anomalySignature at :1004; all-clear path emits a health ping every observerHealthEvery=4 cycles at :2086-2094.

steps.label: runAgentTurn("observer", prompt) — Observer LLM turn on the anomaly set
steps.detail: On a changed anomaly set the orchestrator calls runAgentTurn(ctx, sid, "observer", buildObserverPrompt(...)) at act-agent/internal/app/orchestrator.go:2101, :2138; whether the LLM produces a faithful anomaly report (vs hallucinating/missing one) is model behavior, not code-enforced — the snapshot data and rules feeding it are real.

steps.label: Observer output → autoRoutePlannerV(role=observer, variantAnomaly) → Planner turn
steps.detail: The agent-message handler matches role "observer" and calls go o.autoRoutePlannerV(ctx, role, content, variantAnomaly) at act-agent/internal/app/orchestrator.go:1215, :1251; the chain is one-way (Planner replies are not re-routed) and is rate-limited by a sliding window — recentAutoRoutes pruned to autoRouteWindow, dropped past autoTurnCap — at :1318-1331.

flows.label: Coordination events → ChronLog → PVM index → PVM search → Planner (decompose)
flows.summary: Every coordination action appends a JSONL event to ChronologicalLog; PVMIndexer polls the log every 10s and batch-stores new events into the vector store; GET /api/pvm/search runs a semantic query against that store. The Planner reaches this evidence via the act_cli pvm search subcommand (real CLI → real endpoint), but the decision to search during decomposition is prompt-instructed, not code-forced. (Note: the Runner ALSO consumes /api/pvm/search to inject patterns into swarm-agent task prompts — a separate consumer of the same store.)

steps.label: chronologicalLog.append(event) — append-only JSONL
steps.detail: Coordination handlers append events throughout server/src/index.ts (e.g. A2A push :239, complete :732, submit-for-validation :858, verdict :892, synthesis :950); ChronologicalLog writes to jsonlPath './data/coordination-log.jsonl' and its append is documented as 'the ONLY way to add events (append-only)' at server/src/services/ChronologicalLog.ts:44-45, :133-135.

steps.label: PVMIndexer.indexNewEvents every 10s → vectorStore.batchStore
steps.detail: pvmIndexer.startIndexing(10000) is called at server/src/index.ts:1596; the setInterval calls indexNewEvents which queries the ChronologicalLog with a since-cursor and batchStores new events into the vector store at server/src/services/PVMIndexer.ts:108-110, :129-151, :211.

steps.label: GET /api/pvm/search?query&limit&project → pvmIndexer.search → vectorStore.search
steps.detail: The endpoint validates query, parses limit/project scope, and returns pvmIndexer.search(query,limit,projectName) results at server/src/index.ts:1178-1192; PVMIndexer.search delegates to vectorStore.search (LocalEmbeddingVectorStore, real all-MiniLM embeddings) at server/src/services/PVMIndexer.ts:318-323.

steps.label: Planner act_cli {subcommand:pvm,args:[search,<q>]} → cmdPvmSearch → routing evidence
steps.detail: The act_cli plumbing is real — cmdPvmSearch fetches /api/pvm/search and prints scored results at act-agent/cli/act-cli.ts:707-744 (dispatch + project scoping) — but the Planner's use of it 'for routing evidence during decomposition' is instructed in prompt text only (planner.go:111, :122 and the on-demand evidence_routing section planner_section_evidence.go:9-50); the LLM decides whether/when to search, and the Planner toolset gives it act_cli (tools.go:76) so the call is possible, not forced.

flows.label: A2A task push → ACT server → targeted swarm role
flows.summary: A caller (Planner/external) POSTs a task to a specific agent id; the server creates the task pre-assigned to that agent, marks it assigned, appends a task_assigned ChronLog event, and emits a Socket.io task_assigned. The targeted swarm Runner then picks it up via its poll loop (Socket.io is fire-and-forget; the actual delivery to the swarm agent is the Runner's REST poll + spawn, not the socket event).

steps.label: POST /api/agents/:agentId/tasks {title,description,spil,priority,requiredCapabilities,projectName}
steps.detail: The A2A push handler at server/src/index.ts:221-254 reads the body and creates a task via taskCoordinator.createTask with assignedAgent=agentId (:227-233); section comment 'Planner pushes a task to a specific agent via A2A' at :220. Whether the in-process Planner actually emits this REST call (vs the CREATE_TASK marker path) is not exercised by the orchestrator's parser — A2A push is the documented external/targeted entry, so the from=planner edge is the intended caller.

steps.label: createTask(assignedAgent) + updateTaskProgress(status:assigned) + chronologicalLog.append(task_assigned)
steps.detail: After createTask the handler calls taskCoordinator.updateTaskProgress(task.id,{status:'assigned'}) and chronologicalLog.append({type:'task_assigned',message:`A2A task push: ${task.id} -> ${agentId}`}) at server/src/index.ts:236, :239-245 — task state lands in TaskCoordinator and the event lands in ChronLog.

steps.label: io.emit('task_assigned',{taskId,agentId,task}) — Socket.io notify (fire-and-forget)
steps.detail: The handler emits io.emit('task_assigned',{...}) at server/src/index.ts:248; this is a best-effort push ('if agent is connected, it gets notified immediately', :247) — it does not by itself deliver work, the Runner's REST poll is the reliable path.

steps.label: Runner poll picks assigned task → fetchPVMContext + buildTaskPrompt → spawn swarm agent
steps.detail: The targeted Runner (one process per swarm role; developer shown as representative) consumes the assigned task and builds the spawn prompt — scoreComplexity>COMPLEXITY_THRESHOLD(4) triggers fetchPVMContext(task) (GET /api/pvm/search) and buildTaskPrompt injects it — at act-agent/runner/act-runner.mjs:361-367, :561-564, :593, :648-656; the actual swarm role spawned depends on which role's Runner owns agentId (re-grep DefaultCapabilities for the live role set).
